title: Fast-path local queue with heterogeneous batching and spill-to-object-storage for console metrics ingest
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a low-latency, tenant-isolated local queue component for the console metrics ingest path that supports heterogeneous batching (per-route batch sizing), low-jitter dequeue, and an overflow spill-to-object-storage fallback. The goal is to reduce p50/p95 tail for small interactive traces while keeping per-token compute efficiency for heavy bursts and avoiding head-of-line blocking from noisy tenants.
activity: 2026-02-10: Initial pitch and problem statement added. Observed sources: high p95 during tenant microbursts, hotkey amplification in multitenant ingest, and frequent memory pressure events on ingress workers.

2026-02-15: Architecture RACI sync with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to keep queue in-process for p50 critical path and provide a non-blocking spill path to S3-compatible storage for excess payloads.
2026-02-18: Prototype queues implemented in ingress-worker v0.1 (branch: feature/fast-path-queue). Prototype supports heterogeneous batch windows keyed by route and request_size_estimate header.

2026-02-22: Load test against production-like workload (50k rps, 20% small traces). Results: p50 improved 18%, p95 improved 12% at 99th percentile CPU. Observed increased S3 writes during heavy bursts; decided to add adaptive retry + coalescing to spill producer.

2026-02-26: Design decision: use leaky-bucket admission into in-memory queue with per-tenant soft caps and a global low-latency fast-path lane. Backpressure will advertise via 503 with Retry-After when spill queue and S3 are saturated.
2026-02-27: Security reviewed spill format with privacy team; agreed to encrypt spilled payloads using existing KMS envelope flow and tag with tenant-id metadata for retention policy enforcement.

2026-03-01: Code review opened for batching scheduler and spill coalescer (PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/892). Tests added for fairness between heavy and light tenants. Performance tests scheduled in staging cluster next week.

Next steps: complete PR review, run interregion soak with synthetic hotkey storm, add dashboards for spill-rate and per-tenant queue occupancy, and document emergency toggle for immediate disable in prod.
comments: Lena Fischer (runtime): We should ensure that heterogeneous batching can be configured per-model route; otherwise model variance will ruin the latency gains. Diego: added per-route config and default heuristic based on recent token length distribution.
Marcus Lee (infra): Can we reuse the existing ingress persistence abstractions? Asha: reused object-store client and metrics tags; created a small adapter to preserve existing audit trails.

Priya Nair (PM): Ensure Console UX reflects when spills occur for tenants—customers care about retained vs dropped metrics. Action: add telemetry->console spike to show spill counts for tenant admins.
Security (audit): Confirmed KMS envelope is sufficient; requested a retention proof point for spilled data. Added to acceptance criteria.
Review note: PR #892 flagged a non-deterministic test in the coalescer. Diego: flake fixed by adding deterministic clock in test harness.
